isolation.sources: own clean neuroscience state plus public external sources only

actions: Audited the public KempnerInstitute/traveling-waves-integrate repository for matched wave-destruction/no-wave interventions. Repository code exposes local convolutional recurrent baselines and wave-related models, but no explicit parameter-matched phase randomization, propagation blocking, recurrent-kernel scrambling, or comparable causal wave-removal intervention was located by repository search. The existing time-series-vs-last-state and wavelength/performance evidence therefore remains supportive but not causal isolation of traveling waves.

Re-verified the Fisher-information-diffusion lead against the accepted ICML 2026 listing and the public pre-acceptance manuscript. The accepted title is Information dynamics and Memory in Neural Networks through Fisher Information Diffusion. The manuscript uses four independent seeds for copy/sequential classification figures, fixes recurrent weights for Sequential-MNIST/CIFAR10/IndoorCVPR classification, trains the readout, and compares Fisher-optimal initialization against Xavier, Kaiming, orthogonal, and unitary schemes. Exact final plotted accuracies remain unrecovered from accessible text, so the candidate stays deferred rather than being numerically promoted.

Added a new peer-reviewed neuroscience-to-AI candidate: Astrocyte-Gated Multi-Timescale Plasticity (AGMP), Frontiers in Neuroscience, published 27 January 2026. Audited online-learning rule, class-incremental results, five-seed protocol, component ablations, timescale sweep, replay assumptions, code/data availability statement, and locality limitations.

new_or_updated_candidates.mechanism: A slow astrocyte-like per-neuron state integrates local membrane potential, synaptic input and spiking activity; after layer-wise normalization a sigmoid gate modulates synaptic updates driven by a local eligibility trace and a fixed-random broadcast error. The design creates a fast eligibility timescale plus slower metaplasticity timescale intended to stabilize old knowledge without replay.
evidence: Frontiers in Neuroscience original research article, published 27 January 2026; all reported experimental results are averaged over 5 random seeds.

Standard online benchmarks: N-MNIST 99.10%, DVS Gesture 95.40%, N-Caltech101 73.80%, CIFAR10-DVS 78.50%, SHD 80.10%. Reported online baselines include e-prop 66.40% on N-Caltech101 and 76.20% on SHD, OTTT 76.27% on CIFAR10-DVS and 77.33% on SHD, and S-TLLR 75.60% on CIFAR10-DVS and 78.23% on SHD.
Class-IL Split N-MNIST (5 tasks): AGMP average accuracy 82.60%, forgetting 15.40%; EWC 72.40/24.50, SI 71.80/25.10, GEM with explicit replay 88.50/8.20.

Class-IL Split CIFAR-100 (10 tasks): AGMP average accuracy 31.40%, forgetting 55.70%; EWC 17.25/61.20, SI 17.26/62.50, LwF 24.20/65.80, GEM with explicit replay 45.20/35.10. Structural SNN methods reported in the comparison table reach substantially higher accuracy but do not all report the same forgetting metric.

Component ablation on Split N-MNIST: full AGMP 82.6%; without astrocytic gate 51.3% (-31.3 points), without eligibility trace 60.2% (-22.4), without homeostasis 68.4% (-14.2). On SHD, removing the eligibility trace lowers 80.1% to 58.3% (-21.8), while removing the gate only lowers stationary-task accuracy to 79.5% (-0.6), supporting a specific stability role for the slow gate rather than a generic accuracy boost.
Timescale sensitivity: best stability is reported when the astrocyte timescale is roughly 50x-500x longer than the eligibility timescale; making it too slow causes under-plasticity.

The learning rule is online in time and does not store the full temporal history; the paper reports an approximately constant 0.9 GB memory footprint for its ResNet-18 setup and about 40% fewer SynOps than standard BPTT in its analysis.
scope: The astrocyte mechanism is biologically inspired, not a direct experimental derivation: the authors explicitly hypothesize that slow astrocytic integration can serve as a contextual stability/metabolic signal.

Spatial locality is incomplete because hidden layers receive a global/top-down teaching signal through fixed random broadcast matrices; the paper itself identifies more biologically plausible feedback as future work.

Class-incremental evaluation uses predefined Split N-MNIST and Split CIFAR-100 task sequences. The gate evolves continuously, but the benchmark setup is not evidence of task-free open-world boundary discovery.

No explicit replay buffer is required by AGMP, but some stronger comparison methods use structural expansion/self-organization and achieve higher CIFAR-100 accuracy; AGMP should not be described as state-of-the-art across all compared continual-learning methods.

Data availability says contributions are contained in the article/supplement and directs further inquiries to the authors; an exact-title GitHub repository search in this run found no implementation repository. Treat independent reproducibility and implementation availability as unresolved.
Efficiency numbers are paper-level analytical/experimental reporting; no independent neuromorphic hardware deployment or wall-plug energy measurement was established in this run.

deferred.lead: Information dynamics and Memory in Neural Networks through Fisher Information Diffusion (ICML 2026 Spotlight)
evidence_recovered: Official ICML 2026 downloads index lists the accepted title.
Public manuscript states Sequential MNIST feeds all 784 pixels sequentially, fixes the recurrent weights in the structured RNN, and trains only a tanh-MLP readout.
Supplementary captions report four independent seeds for the copy task and sequential CIFAR10/IndoorCVPR comparisons against Xavier, Kaiming, orthogonal and unitary initializations.

The manuscript explicitly limits full theory to simple RNNs; an LSTM experiment applies Fisher-optimal initialization only to recurrent gate matrices and is empirical transfer, not theoretical optimality of LSTMs/GRUs.
deferred.unresolved: Exact final-version plotted losses/accuracies and code/artifact provenance remain to be recovered before promotion.

qualified.lead: Traveling Waves Integrate Spatial Information Through Time causal interpretation
qualified.reason: Repository audit still found no clean parameter-matched intervention that selectively destroys propagation/waves while preserving local recurrence, parameter count and optimization. Keep time-series-readout gains, wavelength correlation and emergent LSTM waves as supportive evidence rather than causal isolation.

qualified.lead: AGMP as fully local biological learning
qualified.reason: Eligibility traces and astrocyte-like gate are local, but the learning signal uses a global error broadcast through fixed random matrices.
The reported continual-learning benchmarks are predefined class-incremental task sequences; continuous gating does not demonstrate autonomous task-boundary inference.

frontier: Find or design a matched traveling-wave intervention: same local recurrent architecture and parameter count, but phase/randomized or propagation-blocked dynamics, with identical optimization and readout. Prefer public artifacts or independent reproductions over post-hoc correlation.

Recover final ICML 2026 Fisher-information-diffusion figure values and code/artifact provenance; if source code is unavailable, extract numeric values from official final figures without inventing precision.

Search for AGMP implementation code, independent reruns, failure reports, and whether its Split CIFAR-100 protocol uses explicit task-boundary resets or state carryover details not obvious from the article text.

Search for experimentally grounded astrocyte/metaplasticity mechanisms transferred into non-spiking deep networks or agent learning with matched component ablations, especially task-free distribution shifts.
Continue language/audio/control/long-context wave or information-propagation ablations with matched parameter counts.
exact_next_action: Prioritize an implementation/reproduction audit of AGMP (code, exact continual-learning protocol, task-boundary/state-reset behavior, and independent reruns); in parallel continue recovering official final ICML-2026 Fisher-information-diffusion numeric figure values, then return to matched wave-destruction experiments.
